x: But his course of antibiotics is now completed, his toe has mended, he has a 10k win under his belt and a new year beckons. There’s more fitness to be gained yet – but it looks as if “Wardy” is back.
Our own Wardy was on cruise control with Bedford's runner, in second, clocking an identical time and the winning margin remained a huge 6 minutes 47 seconds.

It was bronze again the following year as only two relics survive (Me and Wardy – if you can call a 23-year-old a relic!) Surely no-one survives from the silver medal team of 1999 … but one does – even if he did memorably break the two cardinal rules of relay-running: don't get lost, and don't walk.
